headline: BC CONSERVATIVES WIN FIRST GOVERNMENT IN 98 YEARS — DRIPA Repeal Tops Mining Industry Wish List
snippet: The British Columbia Conservative Party won a decisive majority on October 24, ending 98 years without a Conservative provincial government. Mining industry associations have welcomed the win, with faster permit processing and repeal of the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA) at the top of the agenda — a significant relief for junior explorers who have faced compounding permitting delays since the BC Court of Appeal's December 2025 ruling that the province's mineral-staking laws violate First Nations consultation duties.

headline: FIREFLY METALS HITS ANOTHER VMS AT GREEN BAY — 22.5M AT 2.5% CuEq, 9.0M AT 3.9% CuEq AT NEW MOUNT JOY ZONE
snippet: FireFly Metals (TSX/ASX: FFM) announced a significant new copper-gold VMS discovery at its Mount Joy zone within the Green Bay project in Newfoundland and Labrador. Best hole FFR26-071 intersected 22.5 metres at 2.5% CuEq including 9.0 metres at 3.9% CuEq, extending the known Noranda-type volcanic massive sulphide system beyond existing resource boundaries and opening a new exploration front at the project.

headline: AGNICO EAGLE AND KINROSS REPORT Q3 TOMORROW — Barnat Pit Failure, $1,730 AISC and Full-Year Guidance Cuts Are the Numbers to Watch
snippet: Agnico Eagle Mines (TSX/NYSE: AEM) and Kinross Gold (TSX/NYSE: KGC) both report Q3 2026 results on October 28 after market close. For Agnico, the Barnat open pit rock-mass movement at Canadian Malartic cut full-year production guidance to the low end of 3.3–3.5 million ounces with 60,000–80,000 ounces lost in H2 — raising the question of how that lands in AISC. Kinross is navigating guided AISC of approximately $1,730 per ounce (+/-5%), among the highest in the senior producer peer group.

headline: FRESNILLO SILVER DOWN 11.5% YTD — World's Largest Primary Silver Miner Needs 10M+ Oz in Q4 to Hit Low End of Guidance
snippet: Fresnillo (LSE: FRES) reported 32.4 million ounces of silver in the first nine months of 2026, down 11.5% year-on-year, primarily due to the end of the Silverstream royalty agreement and lower grades at Juanicipio and Cienega. With full-year guidance maintained at 42.0–46.5 million ounces, the world's largest primary silver producer needs between 9.6 and 14.1 million ounces in Q4 alone — a sharp sequential ramp — to reach even the low end of the range.

headline: HAWK RESOURCES DRILLS 19.7M AT 1.2% CU, 1.4 G/T AU — Seven of Ten Holes Mineralized at Utah Cactus Corridor
snippet: Hawk Resources reported significant copper-gold-silver mineralization in seven of ten holes at its Cactus Corridor project in Utah, with the best intercept returning 19.7 metres at 1.2% copper and 1.4 g/t gold near surface. The results confirm broad, near-surface copper-gold zones with commercial-grade potential across the project, adding a new porphyry-style exploration-stage copper-gold asset to the junior mining market.

headline: KANTRA COPPER LIFTS KANMANTOO RESERVE 31% — New Emily Star Underground Ore Body Adds Second Mining Front
snippet: Kantra Copper's updated mineral reserve at Kanmantoo in South Australia rose 31% to 5.2 million tonnes after accounting for all mining depletion, while a maiden underground reserve at the Emily Star deposit adds 740,000 tonnes at 0.91% copper as an entirely new mining front. The dual-source reserve growth signals the project's longevity extends well beyond the current open pit mine plan.

headline: STONEX WEEKLY: GOLD-SILVER WASH-OUT DEEPENS — Russian Official Selling Joins 10.5-Tonne ETF Exodus as Pre-FOMC Sentiment Sours
snippet: StoneX's October 26 precious metals weekly round-up identifies a broadening institutional 'wash-out' in gold and silver, with Russian official sector selling emerging alongside 10.5 tonnes of net ETF redemptions in a single week. The firm notes the correction has retraced the most speculative positioning built since gold's January 2026 all-time high and says sentiment has turned markedly sour ahead of Wednesday's FOMC decision, even as gold holds above the $4,000 level.

headline: GOLDSILVER.COM: GOLD CORRECTION HIT PORTFOLIOS — But Holders Who Bought Pre-Rally Are Still Up 40%
snippet: GoldSilver.com's analysis of the 2026 gold correction puts the pullback in context: holders who entered before the January 2026 all-time high are still sitting on 40% or more in gains at current prices near $4,000, which limits the panic-selling impulse that defined earlier corrections. The piece argues the more significant risk for retail investors is the widening discount of gold mining equities to bullion — a divergence that has historically preceded either a metal pullback or an equity re-rating.

headline: BARRICK Q3 PREVIEW: AISC GUIDANCE $1,760-$1,950 WITH GOLD AT $4,000 — Margin Math Gets Uncomfortable
snippet: Zacks previews Barrick Mining's upcoming Q3 2026 results against a wide guided AISC range of $1,760–$1,950 per ounce — one of the broadest bands in the senior-producer peer group and a figure that significantly compresses margins when gold trades near $4,000. With Barrick the last major gold producer to report in the current earnings cycle, the question is whether the wide range reflects genuine operational uncertainty at Pueblo Viejo or a conservative bias that may allow results to beat.

headline: FXEMPIRE: SILVER NEXT SUPPORT $49-50 — Gold Faces $3,600 in Bear Scenario if Fed Surprises With December Hike
snippet: FXEmpire's pre-FOMC technical analysis identifies $49–50 as the next meaningful support for silver after the metal fell to two-month lows, while a hawkish surprise that sparks a December rate-hike expectation could push gold to $3,600 — roughly 10% below current levels. The base case remains a Fed hold at 3.75–4.00% with neutral language, expected to trigger a modest gold recovery toward $4,075 resistance.

headline: KE REPORT: BRIEN LUNDIN SEES JUNIOR FINANCING BOOM FORMING UNDER GOLD'S CURRENT PAUSE
snippet: Gold Newsletter editor Brien Lundin tells the KE Report that the current gold consolidation is a digestion phase rather than a trend reversal, and identifies a building junior mining financing boom as the most actionable signal for retail investors. Lundin argues the disconnect between strong metal prices and explorers/developers down 30–50% creates multi-bagger setups for investors who pick companies with funded drill programs and targets the market has not yet priced in.
